## The Neuro-Symbolic Trust Boundary

Naive "LLM-writes-R-code" tools execute untrusted model output directly via
`eval(parse())`, creating severe reproducibility, statistical correctness, and
security vulnerabilities. `specshiny` enforces a strict **neuro-symbolic trust
boundary**:

1. **Declarative IR Only**: Translators (`translator_rule()`,
   `translator_openai()`, `translator_ollama()`) produce a declarative data
   structure (`spec_ir`), never executable code.
2. **Pure-R Schema & Guardrail Gate**: `validate_spec_ir()` rejects unknown
   nested JSON properties, non-ASCII or reserved identifiers, non-positive-definite
   correlation matrices, unidentifiable random slopes, and unsafe parameter grids.
3. **Static Positive-Allowlist AST Verification**: Every script emitted by
   `compile_r_script()` must pass `verify_compiled_r_ast(code, strict = TRUE)`,
   proving statically that only whitelisted statistical and base functions are
   called.
4. **Sanitized Reports & Verifiable Study Bundles**: `compile_quarto_report()`
   neutralizes inline knitr expressions, code-fence breakouts, HTML/XSS, and
   dangerous LaTeX directives, while `export_spec_bundle()` and
   `verify_spec_bundle()` pair SHA-256 checksums with AST attestation.

## 1. Closed Schema & Pure-ASCII Identifier Guardrails

```{r}
library(specshiny)

base <- new_spec_ir()
base$schema_version

# Attempt to smuggle an unknown nested property from an LLM JSON payload
raw_obj <- jsonlite::fromJSON(as_spec_json(base), simplifyVector = FALSE)
raw_obj$hierarchy$injected_hook <- "system('id')"
v_extra <- validate_spec_ir(as_spec_ir(raw_obj, validate = FALSE))
v_extra$valid
v_extra$errors[, c("path", "code", "category")]
```

Identifiers are restricted to pure ASCII (`<= 64` bytes, non-reserved),
blocking code injection, leading dots, and Unicode homoglyphs:

```{r}
s_bad <- base
s_bad$outcome$name <- "y; system('id')"
validate_spec_ir(s_bad)$errors[, c("path", "code")]

# YAML !expr evaluation tags are blocked even when yaml.eval.expr = TRUE
evil_yaml <- "schema_version: !expr \"stop('NEVER_RUN')\"\ndesign_type: monte_carlo_lm\n"
tryCatch(
  parse_spec_text(evil_yaml, format = "yaml"),
  error = function(e) cat("Blocked YAML attack:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
)
```

## 2. Forward-Compatible Schema Migration (`migrate_spec_ir()`)

Specifications archived under schema `v1.0.0` validate with a structured
`schema_outdated` warning and upgrade cleanly to `v1.2.0` via
`migrate_spec_ir()`:

```{r}
legacy <- unclass(new_spec_ir(
  design_type = "multilevel_sim",
  hierarchy = list(levels = 2L, n_clusters = 30L, cluster_size = 15L, icc = 0.2)
))
legacy$schema_version <- "1.0.0"
legacy$hierarchy$cluster_size_dist <- NULL
legacy$outcome$error_dist <- NULL
legacy$effects$interactions <- NULL

validate_spec_ir(as_spec_ir(legacy, validate = FALSE))$warnings[, c("path", "code")]

upgraded <- migrate_spec_ir(legacy)
upgraded$schema_version
attr(upgraded, "migration_log")
```

Attempting to downgrade a future schema version produces a crisp
`specshiny_version_mismatch` diagnostic:

```{r}
future_spec <- legacy
future_spec$schema_version <- "2.0.0"
tryCatch(
  migrate_spec_ir(future_spec),
  error = function(e) cat("Version mismatch:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
)
```

## 3. Static AST Safety Verification (`verify_compiled_r_ast()`)

Every compiled simulation script passes static AST verification automatically:

```{r}
spec <- nl_to_spec(
  "2-level power study with 40 schools, 20 students per school, ICC 0.2, treatment effect 0.35, 50 reps"
)$spec

code <- compile_r_script(spec)
ast_ok <- verify_compiled_r_ast(code)
ast_ok
```

Adversarial scripts attempting direct calls, triple-colon internal access,
dynamic callees, or higher-order banned arguments (`lapply("id", system)`) are
caught statically without ever executing a single line:

```{r}
attacks <- c(
  direct_eval = "eval(parse(text = '1 + 1'))",
  do_call = "do.call(rbind, list(1, 2))",
  higher_order = "lapply(c('id'), system)",
  triple_colon = "stats:::C_Cdqrls",
  bad_package = "library(utils)"
)

data.frame(
  attack = names(attacks),
  safe = vapply(attacks, function(s) verify_compiled_r_ast(s)$safe, logical(1)),
  first_violation = vapply(attacks, function(s) verify_compiled_r_ast(s)$violations$code[[1L]], character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

## 4. Quarto, LaTeX, and XSS Sanitization

Even when untrusted free-text metadata contains inline knitr code, code-fence
breakouts, LaTeX `\write18`, or `<script>` tags, `compile_quarto_report()`
neutralizes every vector before emitting the `.qmd` file:

```{r}
poison <- new_spec_ir(
  title = "Study `r system('id')` \\write18{id} <script>alert(1)</script>",
  source_prompt = "Prompt `r 1 + 1` | table breakout",
  hierarchy = list(levels = 1L, n_obs = 80L),
  simulation = list(n_reps = 5L, seed = 42L)
)
qmd <- compile_quarto_report(poison, execute = FALSE)
c(
  has_inline_knitr = grepl("`r\\s", qmd, perl = TRUE),
  has_write18 = grepl("\\\\write18", qmd, perl = TRUE),
  has_raw_script = grepl("<script", qmd, ignore.case = TRUE),
  uses_six_tilde_yaml_fence = grepl("~~~~~~yaml", qmd, fixed = TRUE)
)
```

## 5. Self-Contained Reproducible Study Bundles

`export_spec_bundle()` writes `spec.yaml`, `simulation.R`, `report.qmd`, and
`bundle_manifest.json` (with SHA-256 digests and AST attestation) into a
path-safe directory, and `verify_spec_bundle()` audits integrity end-to-end:

```{r}
bundle_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "specshiny_safety_vignette_bundle")
export_spec_bundle(spec, bundle_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
ver <- verify_spec_bundle(bundle_dir)
ver

# Inspect manifest checksums and AST attestation
ver$manifest$ast_verification
unlink(bundle_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
